Hanul lui Manuc · Bucharest

An inn for a
whole neighbourhood.

Une auberge pour tout un voisinage.

Built in 1808 by the Armenian merchant and diplomat Manuc Bei, this courtyard gave Bucharest a room where trade, travel, politics and hospitality could meet.

A city of arrivals

Before the nation, there was the table.

An inn is a practical architecture of trust: a place to sleep, bargain, eat, exchange news and wait for a decision. At Manuc’s Inn, the city’s Armenian, Ottoman, Balkan and Romanian worlds were not an abstract lesson in “diversity.” They were the daily conditions of urban life.

Une auberge est une architecture concrète de la confiance : on y dort, on négocie, on mange, on échange des nouvelles et l’on attend une décision. À l’auberge de Manuc, les mondes arménien, ottoman, balkanique et roumain de la ville ne relevaient pas d’une leçon abstraite de « diversité » : ils formaient le quotidien urbain.

1808

A house with many doors.

Manuc Bei’s inn was made for movement: merchants and travellers, languages and currencies, official errands and private bargains. Its courtyard is an argument against a purified past. Romania did not begin outside the region; it learned how to remain itself within it.

1812

Diplomacy comes indoors.

The Treaty of Bucharest, which ended the Russo-Ottoman war, was signed at the inn. Its consequences—including Russia’s acquisition of Bessarabia—were felt far beyond its rooms. A house of hospitality became a witness to the pressure of empires.

Le traité de Bucarest, qui mit fin à la guerre russo-ottomane, fut signé à l’auberge. Ses conséquences — dont l’acquisition de la Bessarabie par la Russie — dépassèrent largement ses murs. Une maison d’hospitalité devint le témoin de la pression impériale.

To face west does not require
forgetting the road behind.Se tourner vers l’Ouest ne demande pas d’oublier la route parcourue.
